newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gold closes at day's low despite New York rises.
newsitem.headline: HK gold closes at day's low despite New York rises.

text.p: Gold was dumped in Hong Kong on Thursday as dealers in the colony were lost for inspiration and found themselves chasing the market down.
Hong Kong gold extended early losses to close at the day's low despite a rebound in New York overnight, dealers said.
Hong Kong bullion ended at US$368.70/369.20 an ounce against New York's US$370.70/371.20 close on Wednesday.
"Morning trade kicked off with sales from Japanese traders due to the U.S. dollar's depreciation," a senior gold dealer said.
Rumours of central bank selling during the Asian day came in at around $370, a European bank dealer said.
"At that moment, the market still believed gold could hold over $370," he said. "But as the market waited, no buying emerged -- that's why people started long liquidation."
Professionals who looked to New York levels as a buying opportunity were disappointed, dealing sources said.
But, one added, "we're not going below $366 yet".
Trading was expected to be choppy on Friday, in a range of $366 to $369 an ounce, dealers said.
"The market is still weak," said a dealer at a local securities house.
Support was generally seen at around $367 to $368, but some dealing sources felt gold could test $362.
Local gold ended HK$2 lower at HK$3,406 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped from +5 to -5.
